text:
Bitcoin exhibits relative weakness near $63,300, failing to capitalize on yesterday's benign U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) report. Despite annual inflation cooling to 3.4% and the core rate easing to 2.5%, the market remains suppressed by localized sell pressure from a recent $90 million hardware wallet exploit and shifting institutional capital.

Notably, leading market maker GSR has aggressively recalibrated its model portfolio, slashing its Bitcoin allocation to 16.9% while elevating Solana (SOL) to its largest holding at 43.6%. This rotation highlights a growing institutional preference for higher-beta smart contract platforms over stagnant large-cap assets.

Traditional markets interpreted the CPI data as dovish, scaling back probabilities of a September Federal Reserve rate hike. However, crypto allocators remain strictly defensive, keeping volume low ahead of today's Producer Price Index (PPI) release to confirm whether this disinflationary trend is robust enough to spark a renewed risk-on rally.
